title: M3 Wear OS Apps Design Kit

components.caption: The primary action of a sign-in prompt, with the account glyph Wear's flow expects.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no sign-in page — there is no set, and no private base node either, to point at. This is Horologist's named button for the flow's primary action.

components.caption: The way past the sign-in prompt: continue without an account.
components.noReference: The other half of the sign-in prompt, and the kit publishes neither. Horologist ships it as its own composable because the choice it offers — carry on without an account — is the one Wear's guidance wants given equal weight, not hidden behind the primary button.

components.caption: Pick which account to sign in with — avatar, name and address per row.
components.noReference: No kit set: the kit draws lists and cards, but not the account picker built from them. Horologist's is a `TransformingLazyColumn` of accounts with the avatar, name and address laid out the way Wear's sign-in guidance specifies.

components.caption: What the sign-in flow shows while it is still deciding what to show.
components.noReference: The kit's `Placeholder` sets cover the button, icon button and card; it publishes no placeholder SCREEN. This is the shimmer a sign-in shows while it works out who is already signed in on the phone.

components.caption: The end of the flow: who you signed in as, shown briefly and then dismissed.
components.noReference: Wear Compose publishes `ConfirmationDialog` and the kit publishes `Dialog`, but neither publishes the signed-in confirmation: the avatar, the greeting and the timeout are Horologist's, and it is the composable a sign-in flow actually calls at the end.

components.caption: Highest emphasis; the screen's primary action.
The kit's highlighted style — a filled button in the variant palette.
Medium emphasis, on a tonal container.
Medium emphasis, drawn as an outline over the background.
Lowest emphasis; no container at all, for a button inside another surface.
A short button for a dense screen, with the kit's content and style axes folded in.
A button over an image, with the scrim that keeps its label legible.
A button waiting on the work it started — the kit's loading pattern.

motion.caption: The first button held, then the last: the pressed one swells by the group's expansion width and its neighbours yield it back.

components.caption: Buttons that share a row and expand away from whichever one is pressed.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no button-group set — it draws rows as side-by-side instances of its button sets. This is a Wear Compose component with no kit counterpart.

components.caption: Interrupts to ask for a decision; the kit's button arrangements fold in as cells.
Hands the task to the paired phone, with the progress the wait needs.
It worked: the check drawn on the theme's success container, over curved copy.
It did not: the same overlay in the failure palette, with the library's own glyph.
The overlay an app brings its own glyph to, which is the icon slot this one takes.
The screen-hugging confirm action, curved to the bottom edge of the display.
A long list that skims by section when the rotating bezel is spun hard, instead of crawling.
components.noReference: No kit set, for the same reason `TransformingLazyColumn` has none: the kit's list pages publish the rows, not the scrolling container — and the rotary skim this adds on top is a behaviour rather than a drawn state, so there is nothing in the kit it could be a cell of.

components.caption: Highest emphasis; an icon-only action.
The kit's highlighted style — a filled icon button in the variant palette.
Medium emphasis, on a tonal container.
Medium emphasis, drawn as an outline over the background.
Lowest emphasis; the kit's child style, with no container at all.
A short label as a round action, with the kit's style and size axes folded in.
Where the screen sits in a scroll, drawn against the right bezel.
The value a rotating side button is setting, while it is being turned.
Which page of a horizontal pager is showing, along the bottom of the display.
The same indicator for a vertical pager, drawn against the right bezel.
The Wear list: rows scale and fade toward the edges of the round display.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no list set — its list pages are the row components (list header, cards) rather than the scrolling container. This is the Wear Compose list idiom, and the transformation that scales and fades rows against the bezel is only visible on the real one.

components.caption: The screen frame: curved clock, scroll position, and the bottom action, in their places.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no scaffold: the chrome it arranges — the curved clock, the scroll indicator, the edge button — are separate sets, and the thing that places them is Wear Compose's, not the kit's.

components.caption: The media player, whole: track and artist above, transport controls across the middle, the output-device and overflow buttons below.
components.noReference: The kit's `Media-Player` set (`71575:22328`) is what this reproduces, but its published cell does not EXPORT as the player: `.Base / Media / Album Artwork/Primary NEW` composites over the whole 192×192 and the exported reference is an opaque purple wash with the player nowhere in it. Mapping to it published a comparison against a blurred background, so the reference is withdrawn until the export is faithful. See the note in this file.

components.caption: The player's footer: the output-device button with its volume badge, and the overflow. Two 44×32 compact buttons in the kit's two 68dp sections.
components.noReference: The kit's `.Base / Media / Footer` (`71575:22221`) — a PRIVATE set, so it carries no coverage row. The published cell it appears in is `Media-Player`, which `Media/PlayerScreen` reproduces whole; this is the same row on its own, so a change to it is diffed without having to read it out of a 192×192 screen.

components.caption: Previous, play/pause, next — the transport row. The track's progress ring is under the middle button's container rather than around it; see the note in this file.
components.noReference: The kit draws the transport row only inside `.Base / Media / Footer` (`71575:22221`), a PRIVATE set the kit walk does not publish and no coverage row can name. The published cell it appears in is `Media-Player`, which `Media/PlayerScreen` reproduces whole.

motion.caption: Seek back, play/pause, seek forward pressed in turn: the pressed button swells and its neighbours yield, the middle button re-morphs on any press, and pausing resolves its scallop to a circle — all over a progress ring that never stops moving.

components.caption: The spoken-word transport row: seek back and forward by a fixed increment.
components.noReference: Horologist's second transport row, for spoken-word playback: the same middle button with seek-back / seek-forward by a named increment either side of it. The kit publishes no podcast cell — its `.Base / Media / Footer` draws the track-skip row only.

components.caption: The middle button: play or pause. Its progress ring is drawn UNDER the filled container rather than around it, so the kit's `Progress=` does not read here — an upstream bug, not a seed. See the note in this file.
components.noReference: The kit's `.Base / Media / Main Control` (`71575:22140`) — a PRIVATE set, so it carries no coverage row. Its `Progress=` and `Playing=` axes are the cells below; its `Shape=` axis is the library's own, scalloped while playing and circular while paused.

components.caption: Track and artist, marquee-scrolled when the title outruns the screen.
components.noReference: The kit's `.Base / Media / Header` (`71575:21983`) — a PRIVATE set. Its text is the kit's own placeholder copy, which `KitCopy.MEDIA_TITLE` / `MEDIA_ARTIST` carry.

components.caption: Jump to the playlist this track came from, with its artwork.
components.noReference: NOT IN THE KIT AT ALL, and this row used to claim it was. The kit's `.Base / Media / Footer` (`71575:22221`) draws two 44×32 compact buttons — `Media/FooterButtons` — not a labelled chip, so there is no cell this reproduces and none to withdraw. It stays on the sheet because Horologist publishes it and a media app that jumps to its source playlist calls exactly this; a reader should just not expect to find it on the kit's player. See the note in this file (issue #67).

motion.caption: The label fades out, the double-pinch glyph springs in and plays, and the label comes back — the button keeps its shape throughout.

components.caption: A button announcing that a double pinch will press it: the label steps aside for the glyph.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no gesture set — one-handed gestures are a design GUIDE (design/ui/wear/guides/patterns/gestures) rather than a component sheet, so there is no frame to compare against. The component is real Wear Compose API, new in 1.7.0-beta.

motion.caption: The scroll rail takes its gesture colours, grows a glyph, and jiggles down and back to show which way a pinch would move the list.

components.caption: The scroll rail growing a glyph: a pinch scrolls the list without the other hand.
components.noReference: The kit's `Scroll-Indicator` set draws the rail alone; the gesture layer over it — the pill, the glyph and the jiggle that says a pinch will scroll — has no cell in the kit, which publishes one-handed gestures as a design guide rather than as a component sheet.

motion.caption: A pill grows above the page dots, plays the pinch glyph, and collapses back into the row.

components.caption: The page dots with the pinch that advances them, along the bottom of the display.
components.noReference: The kit's `Page-Indicator` set draws the dots alone; the gesture pill that grows above them has no cell, one-handed gestures being a design guide rather than a kit component sheet.

components.caption: The same pinch-to-advance affordance for a vertical pager, against the right bezel.
components.noReference: The kit's `Page-Indicator` set draws the dots alone; the gesture pill beside them has no cell, one-handed gestures being a design guide rather than a kit component sheet.

components.caption: Three wheels for a date, with the kit's field orderings folded in.
Wheels for a time, pinned to midnight; the kit's clock formats fold in as cells.
One wheel of options — the primitive the date and time pickers are built from.
A button whose icon and labels have not arrived yet.
An icon button whose icon has not arrived yet.
A card whose icon and text have not arrived yet.
A ring around the display edge, with the kit's progress and stroke axes folded in.
The same ring cut into segments, for progress through a countable set of steps.
An indeterminate arc along the bezel, for a wait with no measurable progress.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no arc indicator: its progress sets are the full ring, the segmented ring and the linear track. This is a Wear Compose component with no kit counterpart.

components.caption: A straight track, for progress inside a component or a list row.
A labelled row that toggles a checkbox; for a set where any number may be chosen.

motion.caption: Flipped on, off and on again: the thumb rides a spring that does not settle the same way in both directions.

components.caption: A labelled row that flips a switch; for a setting that takes effect immediately.
A labelled row in a set where exactly one may be chosen.
The expressive shape library, with each named shape folded in as a variant.
A value across a fixed number of steps, with the kit's levels folded in as cells.
A value moved a step at a time, between buttons at the top and bottom of the screen.
